sentences.text: Stratiotosuchus possessed a robust, laterally compressed skull measuring 47 cm long, equipped with ziphodont teeth that were laterally compressed, curved, and serrated.
Unlike most baurusuchids which typically have four premaxillary teeth, the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — of Stratiotosuchus possessed only three premaxillary teeth.
This animal stood with a fully erect posture similar to that of bipedal theropod dinosaurs.
Preparation of the holotype skeleton revealed evidence of two individuals preserved together in the same sandstone block.
Stratiotosuchus had large crests over its hip socket that stabilized the hip in a pillar-erect stance.
The first fossils of Stratiotosuchus were found in the 1980s, and the type species was named in 2001 by Campos and colleagues.
Stratiotosuchus was a hyperpredator that likely filled ecological niches occupied by theropod dinosaurs in other regions.
It likely had a much stronger puboischiotibialis muscle than modern crocodilians, allowing it to maintain a permanent upright stance.
The arm socket of Stratiotosuchus faced backwards and downwards, suggesting its arms were held beneath the body.
Tightly clustered metacarpals forming narrow hands and a backward-projecting calcaneal tuberosity suggest an erect posture in Stratiotosuchus.
The upper part of the femur in Stratiotosuchus has a rough surface region analogous to the accessory trochanter found in tetanuran theropods.
The articular surface where the tibia attaches to the femur in Stratiotosuchus is laterally compressed, unlike the circular surface in living crocodilians but similar to theropod dinosaurs.
Stratiotosuchus has been classified as a baurusuchid since its first description in 1988 and belongs to the family Baurusuchidae.
It belongs to the clade Metasuchia, which includes living crocodilians and extinct relatives extending back into the Jurassic.
According to Montefeltro et al. (2011), Stratiotosuchus belongs to the subfamily Baurusuchinae within the family Baurusuchidae.
Riff and Kellner (2011) placed Stratiotosuchus deep within Notosuchia as the sister taxon to the family Sphagesauridae.
The parent group of Stratiotosuchus is Baurusuchinae.
Stratiotosuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
Stratiotosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous.
Specimens of Stratiotosuchus come from the Adamantina Formation, which dates to either the Turonian-Santonian (about 85 million years ago) or the Campanian-Maastrichtian (about 70 million years ago).
Stratiotosuchus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
The exact phylogenetic position of Stratiotosuchus within the clade Metasuchia remains uncertain.
